claim_verdicts.evidence: Argo CD overview: "Argo CD follows the GitOps pattern of using Git repositories as the source of truth for defining the desired application state." "Argo CD is implemented as a Kubernetes controller which continuously monitors running applications and compares the current, live state against the desired target state (as specified in the Git repo)." 'Agent inside the cluster' is labelled as the course's setup; staging-manual.yaml destination is https://kubernetes.default.svc (same cluster). 'deploy = a commit' judged under claim 7.

Argo CD overview: "providing facilities to automatically or manually sync the live state back to the desired target state." The course's first Application, deploy/gitops/lessons/staging-manual.yaml: "No sync policy: Argo CD only compares, and syncs when someone asks." So in the course's setup a commit alone does not deploy, and 'nobody runs a command against the cluster' is false until automatic sync is set.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: To deploy a new version, you, or a CI job, change `image:` in `api.yaml` and push the commit; the agent picks up the change from Git. Whether it then applies it on its own or waits to be told is a setting covered later.

issues.text: Overstated: a commit alone deploys only when the agent syncs automatically. Argo CD offers "automatically or manually sync", and the course's own first Application (deploy/gitops/lessons/staging-manual.yaml) has "No sync policy: Argo CD only compares, and syncs when someone asks." The sentence is framed as 'GitOps as this course sets it up', so it is false for the next lesson. Same overstatement in section 3 ('so that deploying means making a commit'), summary line 1 and q1's 'correct' explanation.
issues.quote: To deploy a new version, you, or a CI job, change `image:` in `api.yaml` and push the commit; nobody runs a command against the cluster.
issues.fix: Section 4: 'To deploy a new version, you, or a CI job, change `image:` in `api.yaml` and push the commit; the agent picks up the change from Git. Whether it then applies it on its own or waits to be told is a setting covered later.' Section 3: 'so that a deploy starts with a commit'. Summary 1: '...so a deploy starts with a commit.' q1 explanation.en/vi correct: replace 'nobody runs a command against the cluster' with 'the cluster is not sent anything from outside'.

issues.text: Outline item 5 is only half established. The lesson says CI needs write access to the repository instead of cluster credentials, but never says what the agent itself needs: read access to the repository and rights inside its own cluster. 'Pull also moves the credentials' does not say where they move to (meta notes record this was cut).
issues.quote: Pull also moves the credentials. The agent opens the connection, from inside the cluster to the repository, so nothing outside has to reach the cluster.
issues.fix: After 'Pull also moves the credentials.' add: 'The agent now holds them: read access to the repository, and rights to change objects in its own cluster.' Keep the rest of the paragraph.

issues.text: 'As this course sets it up' ties the general model to the course, but the course's config repository lives on a Git server inside the cluster (staging-manual.yaml repoURL http://gitea.git.svc:3000/donhang/donhang-config.git). There, whoever commits must reach the cluster's Git server, so 'nothing outside has to reach the cluster' and 'CI needs permission to write to the repository, not access to the cluster' describe a repository outside the cluster, such as one on GitHub, not the course's lab.
issues.quote: The bottom path is GitOps as this course sets it up:
issues.fix: Replace 'GitOps as this course sets it up' with 'GitOps in its usual form', and in the credentials paragraph write 'The agent opens the connection, from inside the cluster to a repository outside it, such as one on GitHub, so nothing outside has to reach the cluster.'

issues.text: 'kubectl scale' is not in my vocabulary or prereq summaries. I only guess from 'shows one replica ... still says two' that it changes a Deployment's replica count directly in the cluster. The situation, section 4, two misconceptions, q5 and the Try it all rely on it.
issues.quote: Meanwhile someone ran `kubectl scale` on `api` to try something:
issues.fix: Add a half-sentence after the first 'kubectl scale': 'which sets a Deployment's number of replicas directly in the cluster, without touching any file'.

issues.text: The code comment on lines 2-3, which the prose points me to ('Line 3 states the push model'), says 'the kind cluster'. 'kind' is not in my vocabulary; section 2 only says 'the local cluster there'. I cannot be sure kind and that local cluster are the same thing.

issues.fix: In section 2 write 'against the local cluster there (the kind cluster the k8s scripts create)', or in the line-3 sentence add 'the kind cluster, i.e. the local cluster on your machine'.
